items.claim: Onset, close, and the speaker-composition hold at the bytes, and the unit correctly separates the English attribution at its final verse from what the Hebrew itself marks.
items.evidence: All five pointed splices re-collate at byte tier against their cited refs. The onset carries the collective reply verb at oshb:Jer.44.15 and the close is bounded by the fresh narrative speech verb וַיֹּ֥אמֶר יִרְמְיָ֖הוּ (oshb:Jer.44.20, byte). The final verse opens וְכִֽי אֲנַ֤חְנוּ מְקַטְּרִים֙ (oshb:Jer.44.19, byte) with no narrative verb of speech, while the translation supplies one, “The women said,” (web:Jer.44.19); refusing to cut there on an English-side attribution is therefore byte-correct, and the whose-mouth question is held rather than decided. Paragraph-mark disclosure is complete for the span: the setumah closing oshb:Jer.44.14 and the petuchah closing oshb:Jer.44.19 are its only paragraph marks (2 marks; none inside oshb:Jer.44.15-Jer.44.18) (single-witness, tier-3 weak in the Prophets), and no ketiv/qere note falls anywhere in oshb:Jer.44.15-Jer.44.19. One minor gap: a paseq seg stands at oshb:Jer.44.17 inside the span (single-witness, seg layer, count-only) and is not disclosed. The header-shaped three-word skeleton at oshb:Jer.44.16 sits in the people's mouth as a second-person perfect, not as a frame header, and the unit rightly makes no header claim there.

items.claim: The unit is typed as an oracle and carried at high confidence although its own bytes contain no divine first-person speech and no messenger formula, and its stated seam contrast at the following verse is contradicted by its own opening verse.
items.evidence: Across oshb:Jer.44.20-Jer.44.23 every reference to the deity is third-person: אֹתָם֙ זָכַ֣ר יְהוָ֔ה וַֽתַּעֲלֶ֖ה עַל לִבּֽוֹ (oshb:Jer.44.21, byte) and וְלֹֽא יוּכַל֩ יְהוָ֨ה ע֜וֹד (oshb:Jer.44.22, byte); the unit is opened by a narrative speech verb, וַיֹּ֥אמֶר יִרְמְיָ֖הוּ (oshb:Jer.44.20, byte), and the row itself states that no messenger formula opens the stretch. Meanwhile the one messenger-formula stretch in this chapter's closing movement carries the full divine title stack at oshb:Jer.44.25 (a member of a 32-verse stack object; sweep: 32 verses) and is typed prose_sermon, so the two type labels sit inverted against the byte evidence for whose speech each unit reports; no per-bytes type deviation is disclosed here. Second defect: the closing warrant and the device note both say the following verse adds the women beside the men, but this unit's own opening verse already names them side by side, עַל הַגְּבָרִ֤ים וְעַל הַנָּשִׁים֙ (oshb:Jer.44.20, byte). The actual byte change at the next onset is the preposition, וְאֶ֖ל כָּל הַנָּשִׁ֑ים (oshb:Jer.44.24, byte): the women move from being spoken about to being spoken to. The device note's gloss drops that preposition, and its recurrence claim about oshb:Jer.44.24 carries no splice of that verse, so the Hebrew half of the claim is unquoted. Paragraph-mark, paseq and ketiv/qere disclosure for the span is otherwise complete and all four pointed splices reach byte tier.

items.claim: The unit's core evidence holds, but it repeats a byte-contested claim about its opening verse and its seg-layer disclosure covers only one of the three paseq-bearing verses inside its own span.
items.evidence: Verified first: the onset splice at oshb:Jer.44.24 is byte-true; the refrain reopening at oshb:Jer.44.26 does echo the opening imperative with no narrative verb intervening, so the internal-cut rejection is sound; and the divine-title identification is correct, חַי אֲדֹנָ֥י יְהוִ֖ה (oshb:Jer.44.26, byte) being the qamats-pointed title, one of eleven divine-title sites among the thirteen skeleton-token verses and split from the two courtly hiriq sites at oshb:Jer.37.20 and oshb:Jer.38.9 (sweep: 13 verses skeleton-wide, 11 divine) — digit and split both correct. Defect one: the claim that the women are now named beside the men at the onset is contradicted by עַל הַגְּבָרִ֤ים וְעַל הַנָּשִׁים֙ (oshb:Jer.44.20, byte), which already names them together; the byte change is the preposition, וְאֶ֖ל כָּל הַנָּשִׁ֑ים (oshb:Jer.44.24, byte). Defect two: the span carries four paseq segs over three verses — one at oshb:Jer.44.25, two at oshb:Jer.44.26, one at oshb:Jer.44.30 (single-witness, seg layer, count-only) — and the unit engages that layer but discloses only the pair at oshb:Jer.44.26; symmetry on a disclosure object is a sweep, not a single site. Petuchah/setumah disclosure is complete for the span, no ketiv/qere note falls in it, and every pointed splice reaches byte tier.

items.claim: The whole-chapter cap and every digit in this unit are correct, but its closure warrant asserts a formula position that the cited verse's own bytes contradict, at the seam that ends the parent.
items.evidence: The unit says the oracle closes on the neum-YHWH formula. In the source bytes that formula stands mid-verse: נְאֻם יְהוָ֔ה (oshb:Jer.45.5, byte) is followed by וְנָתַתִּ֨י לְךָ֤ אֶֽת נַפְשְׁךָ֙ לְשָׁלָ֔ל עַ֥ל כָּל הַמְּקֹמ֖וֹת אֲשֶׁ֥ר תֵּֽלֶךְ שָֽׁם (oshb:Jer.45.5, byte) — the very life-grant clause the same sentence says the oracle closes on — so the verse's last words are not the formula, and the row's own splice displays this. Under the ruling that this formula is closure corroboration only, a mis-positioned closure citation inflates the evidence exactly at the seam where the parent ends and the nations collection opens. Everything else verifies: the whole-chapter cap posture holds at medium_low with the frontier flag set and a counted cap phrase; the aleph-lexeme digit is byte-correct — the bare token stands in exactly eight verses book-wide, this unit's oshb:Jer.45.3 among them, and a zero-to-two prefix test returns the same eight (sweep: 8 verses; an independent re-sweep reproduces eight, not the ten that circulates in prose summaries of this lexeme) — and it is correctly split from the vav-initial woe and funeral-cry system; the asher-dibber header shape at oshb:Jer.45.1 is byte-distinct from the eleven-verse asher-hayah list (sweep: 11 verses); the header-internal date class is correct; and parashah plus paseq disclosure across oshb:Jer.45.1-Jer.45.5 is complete with no ketiv/qere note in the span.

items.claim: The unit folds a collection-scope rubric into a single-nation oracle without ever testing that rival, and its first-direct-address claim contradicts its own reading of the imperatives eight and two verses earlier.
items.evidence: The rubric is scoped to the whole collection in its own bytes, עַל הַגּוֹיִֽם (oshb:Jer.46.1, byte), plural and naming no nation, while this unit's nation header is lamed-scoped to one nation, לְמִצְרַ֗יִם (oshb:Jer.46.2, byte). The row states that collection scope in prose yet ends the span at oshb:Jer.46.12, and the rejected alternative it does test is a different seam (header to battle-poetry), so the rubric-as-its-own-superscription rival is never engaged even though the controlled vocabulary carries that type and the book's opening superscription is handled as its own unit. Second defect: the address at oshb:Jer.46.11 is called the vision's first direct address, but second-person plural imperatives already stand at עִרְכ֤וּ מָגֵן֙ וְצִנָּ֔ה וּגְשׁ֖וּ (oshb:Jer.46.3, byte) and עֲל֤וּ הַסּוּסִים֙ וְהִתְהֹלְל֣וּ (oshb:Jer.46.9, byte), rendered as commands in both witnesses, and the row's own prose calls them imperatives addressed to unnamed combatants; the defensible claim is first named vocative. Third, smaller: the form quoted at oshb:Jer.46.10 is the lamed-prefixed title stack, its own token object, so the hedge about the bare skeleton token's point-aware split is attached to the wrong object. Verified correct: the four-verse header-shape digit (sweep: 4 verses, the rubric among them); the ketiv/qere disclosure at oshb:Jer.46.11, with both the unpointed written form and the pointed read form present in the source bytes and the note count matching; the petuchah closing oshb:Jer.46.12 and the setumah closing oshb:Jer.45.5 as the only marks at or adjacent to the span (2 marks; none inside oshb:Jer.46.1-Jer.46.11); no paseq seg in the span; the header-internal date class; the resh-family name spelling; and every pointed splice at byte tier.
tier_citations: verse-count sweep (4 verses, asher-hayah header shape)

items.claim: The boundary is well warranted, but the sole ground given for rejecting the strongest rival is false about this unit's own opening verse and rests on an undigited book-wide pattern claim the bytes contradict.
items.evidence: The rejected alternative says the heading carries no content of its own once split from the proclamation it frames. The heading's own bytes carry its topic clause, לָב֗וֹא נְבֽוּכַדְרֶאצַּר֙ מֶ֣לֶךְ בָּבֶ֔ל לְהַכּ֖וֹת אֶת אֶ֥רֶץ מִצְרָֽיִם (oshb:Jer.46.13, byte), which is content and is precisely what makes it a topical header. The generalization backing that rejection — that the book's other prose headers open directly onto their first movement rather than standing as isolated citations — carries no sweep digit naming object or unit, and it is contradicted at three sites of the eleven-verse header list, where the header verse is content-free and the movement begins in the next verse: הַדָּבָר֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר הָיָ֣ה אֶֽל יִרְמְיָ֔הוּ מֵאֵ֥ת יְהוָ֖ה לֵאמֹֽר (oshb:Jer.7.1, byte), byte-identical at oshb:Jer.11.1 and oshb:Jer.30.1. This refutes the heuristic-false-positive disposition recorded against the universal-claim flags on this unit's rejected alternative: those flags mark a real defect, not a matcher artifact. Smaller, secondary: the translation run for web:Jer.46.18 closes its curly pair after the oath opening and carries the remainder of the verse's rendering after a straight double quote with no closing curly before the ref, so only the opening fragment is delimited. Verified correct: the melekh-signature digit (sweep: 3 verses) and its mid-verse position — oshb:Jer.46.18 ends on its Tabor-and-Carmel clause while the two later sites end on the signature itself, so declining a closure-corroboration claim here is byte-right; the dibber-versus-hayah header distinction against all three hayah-built shapes; the paseq at oshb:Jer.46.16 as the span's only seg (1 seg); the petuchah closing oshb:Jer.46.12; no parashah mark and no ketiv/qere note inside the span; and every pointed splice at byte tier.
tier_citations: verse-count sweep (11 verses, asher-hayah header list)

items.claim: The inclusio carrying this unit's framing is overstated at the bytes: the shared element is a construct standing three times in the chapter, its address form recurs across two earlier row seams undisclosed, and the span's closing occurrence is third-person rather than the address its opening verse carries.
items.evidence: A token-bound consonantal sweep of the construct returns three verses, all in this chapter: oshb:Jer.46.11, oshb:Jer.46.19 and oshb:Jer.46.24 (sweep: 3 verses, skeleton tier). The opening verse addresses her in the second person with an imperative, עֲשִׂ֣י לָ֔ךְ ... יוֹשֶׁ֖בֶת בַּת מִצְרָ֑יִם (oshb:Jer.46.19, byte), and the same second-person address with the same construct already stands eight verses earlier at עֲלִ֤י גִלְעָד֙ וּקְחִ֣י ... בְּתוּלַ֖ת בַּת מִצְרָ֑יִם (oshb:Jer.46.11, byte) — on the far side of two row seams and undisclosed here — so the addressee device is chapter-level continuity rather than a span-bounding frame. The closing verse is third-person in both witnesses, הֹבִ֖ישָׁה בַּת מִצְרָ֑יִם נִתְּנָ֖ה (oshb:Jer.46.24, byte), so what returns at the close is the construct, not the address; the framing claim carries no sweep digit anywhere in the unit. Verified correct: the setumah closing oshb:Jer.46.19 disclosed as mid-span texture rather than adopted as a driver, and as the span's only parashah mark (1 mark); the mid-verse position of the closure formula at oshb:Jer.46.23 (the verse runs on to its locust comparison); no paseq seg and no ketiv/qere note in the span; the span-internal negative that no fresh direct address intervenes across oshb:Jer.46.20-Jer.46.24, which is byte-true, so the heuristic-false-positive disposition on that universal-claim flag is confirmed; and every pointed splice at byte tier.
tier_citations: verse-count sweep (3 verses, bat-Mitsrayim construct, skeleton tier)

items.claim: Onset and close are both byte-warranted, the divine-title digit and object are exact, and the disclosure set for the span is complete.
items.evidence: The onset carries a divine speech formula without the particle heading the book's dominant formula, אָמַר֩ יְהוָ֨ה צְבָא֜וֹת אֱלֹהֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֗ל (oshb:Jer.46.25, byte); an independent verse sweep of that full title stack returns thirty-two verses with this site among them (sweep: 32 verses), matching the unit's digit and object, and this chapter carries no koh-amar verse at all, so the stated contrast is byte-true rather than rhetorical. The close is bounded by the addressee change at oshb:Jer.46.27, where the address turns to a covenant addressee in the second person, with no byte-attested continuity marker bridging it. Disclosure is complete: the setumah closing oshb:Jer.46.26 (single-witness, tier-3 weak in the Prophets) is the only paragraph mark at or adjacent to the span (1 mark), and no paseq seg and no ketiv/qere note falls in oshb:Jer.46.25-Jer.46.26. The name spelling at oshb:Jer.46.26 is the resh-family form, the same form attested at oshb:Jer.46.2, and the claim is not extended past those attested sites. Both pointed splices reach byte tier, the closing formula at oshb:Jer.46.26 is quoted without a position claim, and the restoration clause is disclosed as unit-internal rather than treated as a boundary.
